newsitem.title: UK: Russian oil tanker insured for $1.8 million-broker.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil tanker insured for $1.8 million-broker.

text.p: A Russian oil tanker reported to have broken in two in the Sea of Japan has hull insurance of $1.8 million, a spokesman for broker Willis Corroon Group Plc told Reuters.
The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka is insured by Russian company Zaschita, with London-based Black Sea and Baltic, part of Russia's Ingosstrakh, reinsuring 85 percent of the risk.

About two-thirds of the 19,000 tonnes of the C grade medium fuel oil on board the Nakhodka has leaked out and there are fears of environmental damage to Japan's western coastline, a spokesman for Japan's Maritime Safety Agency spokesman said.
The vessel's last position was given as 150 km (90 miles) north east of the Oki Islands.
Nippon Salvage has been instructed to try to salvage part of the vessel which is still afloat, the Willis Corroon spokesman said.
P&I (Protection and Indemnity) insurance, which will cover pollution claims, is provided by the UK P&I Club, the largest of the mutual marine P&I clubs.
The UK P&I Club said it was sending a pollution expert from the International Tanker Owners Pollution Federation to Tokyo to advise on any clean-up operations.
The vessel is owned by Prisco Traffic Limited based in the city of Nakhodka.
No details were available of the cargo insurers.
